function: DDPG-based DRL jointly designs the BS RSMA precoding matrix and the active RIS reflecting matrix, with a constraint-matching function, to maximize energy efficiency (pp. 6-8).
system: Downlink MISO: 8-antenna BS, 10 single-antenna users, 16-element active RIS (4x4), one-layer RSMA, low-resolution DAC/ADC (2-10 bits), 10 MHz; carrier frequency not given (pp. 3, 11).
method: DDPG reinforcement learning, two-hidden-layer networks (1024, 512 nodes), constraint-matching function enforcing power and amplitude constraints, trained 15000 episodes of 200 steps (pp. 7-12).
data_channel: Own simulated Rician BS-RIS and RIS-user channels (array-response LoS, Rayleigh NLoS), path-loss exponent 2.2, users placed randomly 50-200 m; no dataset or measurement (p. 11).
test_conditions: One simulated setup (8 antennas, 10 users, 16 RIS elements); sweeps of RIS size, Rician factor, BS power, quantizer bits; no train/test shift stated (pp. 11-14).
baselines: Non-learned: own SCA alternating method, OFDMA/OMA with active or passive RIS, RSMA with passive RIS, local search (LSA); no learned baseline (pp. 12-14).
metrics: Energy efficiency (bps/Hz/J), spectral efficiency, power consumption, training reward, policy loss, convergence iterations (pp. 12-14).
complexity: DRL inference O(NU + NM + MU) vs SCA alternating O((UM)^3.5 + N^3.5) per iteration; complexity versus users plotted (pp. 11-12, Fig. 3).
q1_support: p. 11: "RIS and users are modeled following the Rician fading channel". Custom Rician channel (array-response LoS, Rayleigh NLoS) with log-distance path loss from [32]; no 3GPP model, public ray-tracing dataset or measured data is used.
q2_support: p. 12: "time-consuming retraining when these scales change". The paper reports retraining for new state and action scales and no test of a trained model in a new scenario; Figs. 6-9 are sweeps of Rician factor, RIS size, power and bits.
q3_support: p. 12: "Then, we simulate the following benchmark schemes to". The benchmarks are QOMA-AR, QRSMA-PR, QOMA-PR (OMA or passive-RIS variants), LSA local search and the paper's own SCA method; all are non-learned and no earlier learned method or other DRL algorithm is compared.
q4_support: p. 11: "Accordingly, the computational complexity of the proposed" DRL algorithm is O(NU + NM + MU), against O((UM)^3.5 + N^3.5) per iteration for the SCA method; Fig. 3 (p. 12) plots complexity against the number of users.
q5_support: p. 11: "To evaluate the proposed solutions and system, we simulate" an environment with an 8-antenna BS and Rician channels; no code or data link, public dataset or measurement is mentioned.
notes: BS precoding and active RIS reflecting matrix are learned jointly with DDPG plus a constraint-matching function (pp. 6-8), so area 3. The SCA alternating method (Proposed-SBA) is non-learned and only assesses the DRL. QRSMA-PR is described as considered in [30] and [31] ([31] is PPO-based) but is a passive-RIS system variant, not a reimplemented learned baseline, hence q3 is 0; reviewer may check. Carrier frequency not stated.
